system_description.narrative_title: Escalation and Militarization Around the Ukraine War
system_description.narrative_summary: The dominant narrative is an accelerating militarization and geopolitical escalation stemming from the Russia–Ukraine war, extending from battlefield advances and drone strikes to economic sanctions, global supply-chain implications, and a nascent arms race that now includes space. Political manoeuvring (domestic politics, truce proposals) and allied responses (sanctions, weapons transfers, air/sea incidents) create reinforcing feedbacks that broaden the conflict's systemic reach and risk spillovers into energy markets, alliance cohesion, and space security.
system_description.scope: The military-diplomatic-economic system directly tied to the Russia–Ukraine war over the news window: battlefield operations, drone and missile strikes, allied military aid and procurement, sanctions/tariff policy, political initiatives toward ceasefires/truces, and emerging weaponization of space.
system_description.super_system: The global strategic order / international security and economic system (great-power competition, multilateral alliances, global markets and supply chains).
adjacent_subsystems: Global arms industry and defense supply chains

variables.name: Battlefield operational intensity
variables.description: Measures the aggregate tempo, scale and frequency of kinetic, aerial and drone operations across the conflict theatre.

variables.name: Military capability balance
variables.description: Measures the relative distribution of combat-ready forces, firepower and sustainment capacity between opposing blocs in the theatre.

variables.name: Arms production rate
variables.description: Rate at which munitions, missiles and military platforms are manufactured or produced for deployment.

variables.name: Weapons transfer flow
variables.description: Rate and volume of cross-border transfers and deliveries of weapons, ammunition and military equipment into the conflict area.

variables.name: Space weaponization level
variables.description: Extent to which offensive or defensive weapon systems and capabilities are deployed, tested or operationally integrated in space.

variables.name: Economic sanctions pressure
variables.description: Intensity and breadth of economic restrictions, financial measures and trade barriers applied to degrade an actor's economic capacity.

variables.name: Energy supply disruption risk
variables.description: Probability-weighted exposure of domestic and international energy supplies to interruption, shortages or price shocks.

variables.name: Alliance cohesion
variables.description: Degree of alignment, coordinated decision-making and operational interoperability among allied actors for security and economic measures.

variables.name: Defense spending level
variables.description: Total fiscal resources allocated to defense procurement, force sustainment and modernization within a given period.

variables.name: Deterrence credibility perception
variables.description: Perceived reliability and effectiveness of punitive or defensive threats to prevent further hostile action.

variables.name: Escalation dynamics
variables.description: Process intensity by which incidents, reprisals or policy moves trigger progressively higher-level military or political responses.

variables.name: Civilian infrastructure vulnerability
variables.description: Susceptibility of power, transport, logistics and critical civilian facilities to damage or functional disruption from conflict-related actions.

variables.name: Humanitarian need level
variables.description: Scale of civilian displacement, casualties and requirement for emergency relief and protection services.

variables.name: Information warfare intensity
variables.description: Frequency, reach and sophistication of disinformation, propaganda, cyber-enabled influence and media operations targeting actors and publics.

variables.name: Supply chain resilience
variables.description: Capacity of critical supply chains to absorb shocks, reroute, and continue delivering essential goods and inputs under stress.

variables.name: Weapon technology diffusion
variables.description: Rate at which new weapon technologies, production methods and tactics spread between actors and into the operational theatre.

catalysts.title: SpaceX Starship orbital test
catalysts.description: Planned first Starship orbital test flight could increase heavy-launch access to orbit and draw attention to space capabilities.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: "SpaceX targets first Starship orbital test on September 22"

catalysts.title: Potential Trump signing of Russia sanctions bill
catalysts.description: Bill passed by the House is awaiting presidential action; a signature would expand tariffs and sanctions powers affecting Russia and third parties.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "House passes sweeping Russia sanctions bill... sends to Trump"; "New US sanctions bill...puts India's Modi in a bind"

catalysts.title: International response to US orbital weapons admission
catalysts.description: US confirmation of weapons in space will likely trigger diplomatic pushbacks and accelerate competitor space programs and doctrine changes.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "U.S. confirms for first time it has weapons deployed in space"; "China warns US space weapons could fuel arms race"

catalysts.title: Ramp-up of Patriot interceptor parts production
catalysts.description: GM and Lockheed Martin moves to produce and fast-track Patriot components will raise defensive production and supply availability.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "Lockheed Martin gets first batch of Patriot interceptor parts from General Motors"; "GM to Produce Patriot Missile Parts"

catalysts.title: Expected Belarus prisoner releases
catalysts.description: US envoy hopes Belarus will release hundreds more prisoners next month, linked to sanctions adjustments and diplomacy.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: "EXCLUSIVE: US envoy hopes Belarus will release hundreds more prisoners next month"; and "Trump's envoy wins release of 25 Belarus prisoners as US drops more sanctions"

catalysts.title: Continuation/expansion of Ukrainian offensive in north Donetsk
catalysts.description: Reported offensive push in north Donetsk is likely to continue near-term, driving local fighting and reciprocal strikes.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "Ukraine launches offensive push in north of Donetsk region"; "Russian strikes injure 18 across Ukraine"

catalysts.title: Attacks on or near nuclear infrastructure
catalysts.description: A drone strike that hit a cooling tower at Kursk plant increases risk of further incidents involving nuclear-adjacent facilities.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: "Drone hit cooling tower on Thursday at Russian Kursk nuclear plant, IAEA says"

catalysts.title: Expansion of anti-ballistic missile/air-defence cooperation
catalysts.description: Poland joining an anti-ballistic missile coalition with Ukraine signals a short-term trend of deeper air-defence cooperation among regional states.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "Poland joins anti-ballistic missile coalition with Ukraine"; "Denmark speeds up Ukraine aid package"

catalysts.title: Acceleration of missile and cheaper munitions production
catalysts.description: Rising European demand and US fast-tracking of missile programs will speed production and deliveries of missiles and related munitions.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "Ukraine war drives European demand for bigger, cheaper missile arsenals"; "Lockheed Martin reveals new secret missile, fast tracks production"

catalysts.title: Continued nationalisation/seizure of Western assets in Russia
catalysts.description: Russia's seizure of Nestlé and Auchan operations signals likely further takeovers or restrictions affecting foreign firms and supply chains.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "Russia Seizes Control of Nestlé’s Local Operations"; "Russia Seizes Control of Nestlé and Auchan operations"
